advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects a git timeout inside a real stage_and_commit (and delete_events), asserting it raises StoreError (not TimeoutExpired) and that the write-lock dir is released afterward.
evidence: test_run_git_folds_timeout_into_a_synthetic_failure asserts only `result.returncode == 124` on `event_append._run_git(...)` in isolation (tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py:100-101), yet its docstring claims 'the caller's existing returncode-inspecting error path fails the write and releases the lock' — a behavior it never exercises.

stage_and_commit converts a non-zero git result into `raise StoreError(...)` inside `with _lock.write_lock(...)` (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:405-424, 425-452); the write_lock release-on-exception path is the actual contract the change relies on and is untested against an injected timeout.

The retry wrappers do NOT treat the rc-124 'git timed out after 30s' stderr as transient (`_with_transient_add_retry` returns immediately on a non-transient result, src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:204-214), so the fold reaches the caller — but a future change to those predicates that re-introduced a hang/raise would pass every existing AC3 test.

ABSENCE: search for `124` / `TimeoutExpired` in the test dir yields only the isolated _run_git assertions; no `pytest.raises(StoreError)` around a stage_and_commit/delete_events call with a timed-out git.
advisory.finding: The store-write timeout recovery contract — a lock-held git timeout during stage_and_commit/delete_events must fold to returncode-124, raise StoreError, and RELEASE the write lock (not raise TimeoutExpired or hang) — is asserted only at the isolated _run_git level; no test drives a real caller with an injected timeout to confirm the clean unwind and lock release.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch event_append.subprocess.run so the lock-held `git commit` raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired, call stage_and_commit on a real tracker, assert `pytest.raises(StoreError)`, and assert the mkdir write-lock dir no longer exists (lock released).

dropped.finding: The ticket's AC1 requires a regression test with a SYNCHRONOUS (not await-based) worker proving the drain bound now fires — the existing test_lifespan_drain_is_bounded explicitly does NOT cover this because it blocks at an await point. Neither new test closes that gap: test_emit_code_review_artifact_runs_off_the_event_loop only asserts a thread-ident difference (that to_thread was used), and test_lifespan_cancel_await_is_bounded_for_a_task_slow_to_cancel blocks with `await asyncio.sleep(3600)` — an await point, the same limitation the ticket calls out.
merged_from: The AC1 regression — that offloading emit_code_review_artifact makes the drain wait_for bound actually fire despite a SYNCHRONOUS (loop-blocking) store write — is not tested; the new test asserts only a thread-id difference, and both it and test_lifespan_drain_is_bounded block at an await point (asyncio.sleep), which is exactly the coverage gap the ticket's AC1 flagged.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the docker-compose comment that _GIT_TIMEOUT bounds each git call and (because a 124 timeout matches no retry marker) a genuine hang short-circuits the retry loops — rather than implying 30s is the whole composed critical-section ceiling.
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:98-108 'The lock-held git work ... is itself bounded by event_append's _GIT_TIMEOUT (30s/call ...) ... the critical section now has an upper bound by construction.'
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:89 `_INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS = 5` and event_append.py:181 `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS = 3` — a single _git_commit composes index-lock x5 * head x3 * add x3, each _run_git 30s-bounded

MITIGATION: event_append.py:246 folds a timeout into returncode 124 with stderr 'git timed out after 30s', which matches none of _TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS/_TRANSIENT_HEAD_MARKERS/index-lock signatures, so a real hang stops after one 30s attempt — the practical bound is ~30s, not 30s*45
dropped.finding: The docker-compose comment now claims a 'provable worst case' bounded by '_GIT_TIMEOUT (30s/call)', but each lock-held git call is composed inside nested retry loops (_with_index_lock_retry up to _INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS=5, _with_transient_head_retry x3, _with_transient_add_retry x3), so the per-call 30s is not the per-commit ceiling. In practice a genuine hang short-circuits (returncode-124 stderr matches no retry marker, so no retry fires), so the bound holds — but the '30s/call' framing understates the composed upper bound and the comment's 'provable' language overstates it.
